title: Design Two-Stage Listing Retrieval and Ranking
prompt: Design a two-stage system that uses user embeddings to retrieve and rank homes a guest is likely to book. Explain training, candidate retrieval, ranking, evaluation, and serving. How would you handle new users and changing availability?

response.placeholder: State your assumptions, then explain your approach and tradeoffs.
response.reference_answer:
This is a practice answer outline, not a reported interview solution.

Clarify the booking objective, request context, inventory constraints and latency budget. Learn user/listing representations from point-in-time interactions, retrieve candidates with an approximate-nearest-neighbor index, apply current eligibility rules and rerank with richer context. Measure the recall cost of filtering after retrieval and over-retrieve or use supported index filters when necessary.

Track retrieval recall separately from ranking quality. Account for exposure bias and delayed booking labels; do not treat every unexposed listing as a negative. Provide context-based fallbacks for new users and content-based embeddings for new listings. Version models and indexes together, refresh availability at serving time, and evaluate completed bookings with latency, cancellation and satisfaction guardrails.
